subject: Fix nine bugs found in review, and put the checks in the repo
body:
Security:
- A forged CF-Connecting-IP was trusted on every request merely because RENDER
  was set. The service's own *.onrender.com hostname is reachable from the open
  internet, so anyone could send that header straight to it and walk past every
  per-IP signup and login limit, while writing addresses of their choosing into
  the audit trail. The header is now trusted only when the hop we are talking to
  is genuinely Cloudflare, checked against their published ranges.
- /auth/set-password let a SUSPENDED account back in. It set status to 'active'
  and, even with that removed, still succeeded and issued a live session cookie.
  It now refuses outright, leaves the password alone and leaves the token unused
  so staff can reinstate and let the link work.
- requireAdmin passed its role check as requireAuth's `next`, so a database error
  inside loadSession surfaced as a 404 and was never logged. Errors now forward.
- /admin/ledger/credit accepted a blank reference. The duplicate guard is a
  partial unique index, which ignores NULLs, so a blank one silently opted out of
  the only thing stopping a double-submitted deposit being credited twice. A
  reference is now required.

Correctness:
- Selecting a customer in the back office never opened the detail panel. wouter
  tracks location.pathname only, so changing just the query string re-wrote the
  URL without re-rendering. Selection is a real route now, and still shareable.
- Google signups dropped the referral code, so anyone arriving on a partner's
  link and choosing Google was recorded with no referrer and the partner lost the
  attribution. They also never got a referral code of their own.
- The signups chart ran a pg `date` through toISOString(), shifting every bar a
  day earlier on any server west of UTC.
- localStorage was read unguarded in a render path; it throws rather than
  returning null when site data is blocked, blanking the whole back office.
- The "not built yet" copy still listed email verification, password reset, KYC
  and withdrawals, all of which now ship.

Also wires the deposit-crediting UI, which had an API client but no caller, and
shows trading-platform status in the back office.

script/test-api.sh is the suite that found the set-password hole, now in the repo
rather than a scratch directory: 42 checks covering the invariants that matter,
including that a reset link cannot escape a suspension, a reference cannot be
credited twice, earnings never count payouts, and a rejected withdrawal returns
the money exactly once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
